title: Take a baseline before any change
statement: Put the measurement in place, check it, and take a baseline before changing a course, because a gain with nothing measured before it can't be shown.
example: One improvement plan ranked its measurement 15th, below the changes it was meant to measure.
detail: An adversarial critique of a plan to improve a reading course found the measurement item ranked 15th, below the changes it was meant to measure, while the course had zero event coverage, and called that the classic optimize-before-instrument error (`grade3-reading/artifacts/alpha-read-packager/v2_final_package/docs/V2_MONSTER_DOSSIER.md`). The plan itself says a baseline snapshot must precede edits, since without the measurement and a pre-edit snapshot even real gains are unmeasurable (the same file), and the project's facts sheet keeps validating the measurement first among the lessons it carries forward (`grade3-reading/artifacts/alpha-read-packager/FACTS_SHEET.md`).

evidence.quote: Ranking the thing-being-measured above the measurement is the classic optimize-before-instrument error.
**Baseline snapshot must precede edits** (#15) — without the Caliper wrapper + pre-edit snapshot, even real gains are unmeasurable.
